item.title: agent-06 · Self-improving AI is a spectrum, not a switch
item.description: A deep dive into AI self-improvement: pseudo-labels, reward shaping, self-defined losses, proposer-solver-verifier loops, and why we are still near the Rubicon.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Yau

item.title: agent-05 · Self-correction has three layers: decoding, workflow, and reasoning
item.description: A deep dive into AI self-correction, from contrastive decoding and external feedback loops to reasoning trained with verifiable rewards.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Yau

item.title: agent-04 · Harness engineering is how we actually make agents useful
item.description: A deep dive into harness engineering: why small models can fail from bad scaffolding, how tools and feedback shape agent behavior, and why agents need more than prompts.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Yau

item.title: agent-03 · What AI agents change about research work
item.description: A deep dive into Hung-yi Lee's lecture on AI agents in academic research: research assistants, idea generation, AI review, and where human judgment still matters.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Yau

item.title: agent-02 · Multi-agent systems are topology problems
item.description: A deep dive into AI agent interactions: collaboration topologies, adversarial games, AI-only social platforms, and why more agents does not automatically mean better agents.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Yau

item.title: agent-01 · Context engineering is the agent's working memory
item.description: A deep dive into Hung-yi Lee's lecture on context engineering: prompt versus context, memory, compression, sub-agents, and agentic context management.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Yau

item.title: agent-00 · The AI agent stack, as seen through Hung-yi Lee's 2026 lectures
item.description: A field guide to six Hung-yi Lee lectures on context engineering, multi-agent systems, harnesses, self-correction, and recursive self-improvement.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Yau
